title: Push the tomli TOML parser past 78 percent kill rate
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 561 mutants in the installed tomli/_parser.py of tomli==2.0.1, the largest single target in this band. Reaching a 78 percent kill rate requires systematic TOML 1.0 spec coverage authored from scratch under work/gc-357/tests/: tables and arrays of tables, inline tables, all four string forms with escape and line-ending edge cases, integer bases, float specials, datetimes, key dotting and redefinition errors -- and the invalid-input half of the spec, asserting TOMLDecodeError on precise malformed documents. The 561-mutant scale forces a staged campaign: partition the parser's grammar into areas, grade after each area lands, triage survivors by ID into a ledger, and re-grade; the suite must stay under 3 seconds throughout or grading disqualifies. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, slow suite, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi tomli==2.0.1 (target under mutation: tomli/_parser.py, the full TOML 1.0 parser)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-357/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-357/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-357/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-357/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-357/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-357/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
